overview.title: Draw text from a trained GPT
overview.summary: Load the model training saved, encode a short prompt with the matching alphabet, and print sampled continuations.

sections.title: Sampling knobs, then any override
sections.pseudocode:
Draw 10 samples of 500 new ids, at temperature 0.8, keeping the top 200.
Seed from 1337 and run configurator.py so flags can retarget the checkpoint.
# Insight: Executing the configurator is how --out_dir=out-shakespeare-char reaches this script.

sections.title: Restore weights and the matching codec
sections.pseudocode:
Resume loads ckpt.pt. A gpt2 name loads that public model with dropout 0.
A character model uses **stoi** and **itos** from meta.pkl.
Otherwise use the gpt2 tokenizer.
# Insight: The codec has to be the one that built the ids. Mixing them produces nonsense.

sections.title: Prompt, then print each sample
sections.pseudocode:
A FILE: prefix means read the prompt from a path, dropping those 5 characters.
Generate without gradients, decode, and print.

logic.title: Draw text from a trained GPT
logic.summary: Load a checkpoint or a published GPT-2, encode a prompt, and print several sampled continuations.

sections.title: Choose how to sample, then apply overrides
sections.pseudocode:
Resume from a checkpoint, unless a GPT-2 name is given.
Read that checkpoint from **out**.
Start the prompt at a newline.
Draw **num_samples** of 10 continuations.
Each continuation adds **max_new_tokens** of 500 ids.
Use temperature 0.8.
Keep only the **top_k** of 200 most likely ids.
Seed both CPU and cuda from 1337.
Run on cuda, in bfloat16 when the GPU supports it, else float16.
Leave compile off.
Run configurator.py, which executes a config file and applies flags.
Allow tf32 matrix multiplies.
On cuda, sample under autocast. On cpu, do not.
# Context: Temperature below 1 makes the next-id distribution sharper. 0.8 is only mildly sharp.
# Insight: The same configurator train.py uses can point this script at out-shakespeare-char.

sections.title: Load a checkpoint, or a published GPT-2
sections.pseudocode:
If resuming:
    Load ckpt.pt onto the device.
    Rebuild the GPT from the saved model args.
    Strip a _orig_mod. prefix on weight names, then load them.
If the name starts with gpt2:
    Load that OpenAI model with dropout 0.
Switch to eval, and move to the device.
Compile only if asked.
# Insight: eval turns dropout off. Sampling with dropout still on would change the distribution every call.

sections.title: Turn text into ids the same way training did
sections.pseudocode:
If the checkpoint names a dataset and that dataset has meta.pkl:
    Read **stoi** and **itos**.
    Encode by mapping each character through **stoi**.
    Decode by mapping each id through **itos** and joining.
Otherwise assume GPT-2 encodings.
Encode with the gpt2 tokenizer, allowing the end-of-text marker.
Decode ids back to text with that same tokenizer.
# Insight: A character-level checkpoint must not be decoded as GPT-2 pieces. meta.pkl is what keeps the alphabet matched.
# Context: stoi maps a character to its integer. itos maps that integer back. prepare.py wrote both.

sections.title: Encode the prompt and print samples
sections.pseudocode:
If the prompt starts with FILE:, read that file as the prompt.
Drop the five-character FILE: prefix to get the path.
Encode the prompt and shape it as one batch on the device.
Without tracking gradients, and under autocast:
    For each sample, generate new ids at this temperature and top-k.
    Decode the first row and print it.
    Print a divider.
# Insight: generate appends ids inside the model. This script only decodes the finished row.
